_meta.title: Mary — National Debt Relief
_meta.why_strong: Hard numbers ($22.8K, $1,020/mo) anchor the persona; emotional JTBD ('get my life back') explicit; demonstrates the 'pay someone to take this off my plate' buying mode that drives debt-relief conversion.

persona.name: Stretched-middle Mary, 42, $22K underwater after divorce
persona.location_context: Mid-size US city, recently divorced, two kids in school, working full-time at $52k/yr, lives in apartment after the house was sold
persona.primary_job: When my minimum credit card payments hit $1,020/month and I'm cutting groceries to pay them, I want to hand this whole mess to a professional who'll deal with the creditors for me, so I can stop opening mail with my heart pounding and get my life back within 2-4 years.

pain_points.label: Monthly minimums are unsustainable
pain_points.description: $1,020/mo across 5 cards + 1 personal loan; eats 25% of take-home; can't save for car repair or kids' activities

pain_points.label: Shame keeps her isolated
pain_points.description: Hasn't told her sister or her best friend; declines invitations to lunch she can't afford; lies about why

pain_points.label: Doesn't know how to negotiate herself
pain_points.description: Tried calling Discover once; got transferred 3 times; hung up in tears; doesn't trust herself to handle 5 different creditors

pain_points.label: Fear of 'sketchy' debt-relief outfits
pain_points.description: A coworker mentioned a debt-relief company that took her money and ghosted; Mary is hyper-cautious of being scammed in this state

trust_needs: 'No upfront fees' stated explicitly (FTC-regulated, but most don't advertise it)
Real customer stories with first names + amounts saved + photos
decision_triggers: A collections call came in to her work phone last Tuesday — she nearly threw up
Free consultation with no commitment (and no credit pull)
Specific monthly payment shown ('You'd pay $X/mo instead of $1,020')
objections: Will this destroy my credit score even more?
How do I know you're not the scam company?
What if my creditors sue me before you negotiate?
persona.channel_behavior: Mobile primarily, late evening after kids in bed; Google search high-intent ('settle credit card debt without lawsuit'); will read Reddit threads about specific company; checks BBB before submitting any form

verbatim_quotes: I just want my life back.
I can't keep doing this — opening the mail makes me feel sick.
I tried calling them myself and I just couldn't.
